questions.prompt: You run GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA main.analytics TO GROUP data_analysts. A colleague creates a new Delta table main.analytics.q4_results the following day. Members of data_analysts query the new table. What happens?

options.label: Query fails — GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA covers only objects existing at grant time; new tables require an additional explicit grant
Query succeeds — GRANT ON SCHEMA automatically cascades to all current and future child objects
Query succeeds only if the table creator also belongs to data_analysts
Query fails because analysts need GRANT SELECT ON CATALOG, not on the schema level

questions.explanation: In Unity Catalog, GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA grants access to objects that existed at grant time. New tables created after the grant are not automatically covered. Administrators must issue an additional grant or configure default privileges for future objects.

questions.prompt: Your team runs hourly ETL pipelines that each take 8 minutes to complete. A senior engineer proposes keeping one all-purpose cluster running 24/7 to eliminate the 4-minute job-cluster startup time. What is the primary cost argument against this approach?

options.label: All-purpose clusters cannot execute scheduled Databricks Jobs — only interactive notebook sessions are supported
The cluster accrues 52 minutes of idle DBU billing per hour to avoid 4 minutes of startup; job clusters start on demand and terminate immediately after each run
Continuous clusters are restricted to a single concurrent Spark job, serializing the hourly pipeline runs
All-purpose clusters reset Spark session state between tasks, causing non-deterministic behavior in scheduled pipelines

questions.explanation: All-purpose clusters accrue DBU costs every minute they run. A 24/7 cluster running 8-minute hourly jobs spends ~88% of its time idle. Job clusters avoid this cost profile by starting fresh per run and terminating immediately upon completion.

questions.prompt: A service principal is granted SELECT on table prod.finance.invoices but has no other Unity Catalog grants. It runs SELECT * FROM prod.finance.invoices and receives a SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND error. What is the most likely missing privilege?

options.label: CREATE TABLE on prod.finance — required even for read-only access to managed Delta tables
MODIFY on prod.finance.invoices — SELECT alone does not allow row-level data access in Unity Catalog
USE CATALOG on prod and USE SCHEMA on prod.finance — without these the three-level namespace cannot be traversed to reach the table
GRANT SELECT must be re-approved by a workspace admin after each cluster restart before it takes effect

questions.explanation: Unity Catalog requires USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA in addition to SELECT on the target table. Without the traversal privileges the SQL engine cannot resolve the fully qualified name even when SELECT is granted, raising a namespace-not-found error.

questions.prompt: Which practices align with designing secure Databricks workloads?

options.label: Apply least-privilege access
Use centralized governance with Unity Catalog
Grant broad owner rights to all users
Run production jobs on the same cluster as ad-hoc notebooks

questions.explanation: Least privilege and centralized governance are core security design patterns for enterprise data platforms.

questions.prompt: A data engineer retrieves a database connection string from a Databricks secret scope and passes it to a Python logging function that writes to the cluster driver log. What does Databricks do with the secret value in that log output?

options.label: Logs the full plaintext value — Databricks only redacts secrets in notebook cell output, not in driver logs
Replaces the secret value with [REDACTED] in driver logs, cluster event history, and notebook cell output
Raises a PermissionError before the secret is passed to the logging function
Encrypts the value in-place with a workspace key before appending it to the log file

questions.explanation: Databricks Secret Scopes redact secret values wherever they appear in Databricks-managed output — notebook cells, driver logs, and cluster event history — replacing them with [REDACTED]. This prevents accidental credential exposure regardless of how the secret is used in code.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at CityMoves Transit. You provision a cluster for the workspace exploration lab. The cluster is idle for 40 minutes with no active Spark jobs or notebook connections. What happens?

cluster_config = {
    "cluster_name": "citymoves-analytics",
    "spark_version": "14.3.x-scala2.12",
    "node_type_id": "Standard_DS3_v2",
    "autoscale": {"min_workers": 1, "max_workers": 8},
    "autotermination_minutes": 30
}

options.label: Cluster terminates automatically because it has been idle longer than autotermination_minutes (30)
Cluster scales down to 0 workers but keeps running to preserve the Spark session context
Cluster switches to SQL Warehouse mode after the autotermination window expires
Cluster sends an idle alert to the workspace admin but continues running indefinitely

questions.explanation: autotermination_minutes = 30 means the cluster shuts down automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity. At 40 minutes idle the cluster will have already terminated, freeing compute and stopping DBU accrual.

db_password = dbutils.secrets.get(
    scope="patient-records-scope",
    key="postgres-password"
)
print(db_password)

options.label: The full plaintext password — Databricks decrypts secrets for the calling notebook and print() outputs the result
[REDACTED] — Databricks masks secret values in all notebook outputs and driver logs
A Python PermissionError because print() is blocked for secret-backed variables in secure workspaces
An empty string because the key has not yet been populated in the scope

questions.explanation: Databricks Secret Scopes redact resolved values wherever they appear in Databricks-managed output, replacing them with [REDACTED]. This prevents accidental credential exposure in cell output, driver logs, and notebook revision history regardless of how the secret is used in code.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at CityMoves Transit. Your team registered public transit data in Unity Catalog. What three-level namespace does this query use?

codeSnippet.code:
SELECT route_id, stop_name, daily_ridership
FROM citymoves_prod.transit_ops.daily_ridership
WHERE trip_date = '2024-03-15'
ORDER BY daily_ridership DESC;

options.label: workspace.database.table — the legacy Hive metastore format used before Unity Catalog
metastore.catalog.object — used for cross-workspace federation queries only
catalog.schema.table — the Unity Catalog three-level namespace: citymoves_prod → transit_ops → daily_ridership
environment.domain.object — used exclusively for external tables backed by cloud storage

questions.explanation: Unity Catalog organizes all data assets in a three-level hierarchy: catalog.schema.object. Here citymoves_prod is the catalog, transit_ops is the schema, and daily_ridership is the table.

questions.prompt: You are building a parameterized deployment notebook for a patient records platform. A Databricks Job task runs this notebook with target_env = 'prod'. What does dbutils.notebook.exit() do in this context?

codeSnippet.code:
env = dbutils.widgets.get("target_env")
catalog = f"{env}_catalog"
schema = f"{env}_patient_data"
spark.sql(f"USE CATALOG {catalog}")
spark.sql(f"USE SCHEMA {schema}")
dbutils.notebook.exit(f"Targeting: {catalog}.{schema}")

options.label: Terminates the Databricks cluster that the notebook is running on
Commits all pending Spark transactions and closes open Delta table writers
Deletes the target_env widget from the current session to prevent reuse in subsequent runs
Returns the string 'Targeting: prod_catalog.prod_patient_data' to the calling Job task so downstream tasks can read it via dbutils.jobs.taskValues

questions.explanation: dbutils.notebook.exit() exits the notebook and returns a string value to the calling context — either a parent notebook that used dbutils.notebook.run() or a Databricks Job task. The calling Job task can then access this exit value through task values for downstream orchestration decisions.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at CityMoves Transit. Your finance team requires cost attribution on all compute resources. You add these tags to the lab cluster configuration. Where do these tags appear after the cluster runs workloads?

options.label: In Azure cost management and billing reports, enabling spend attribution by project and cost center
As metadata columns automatically appended to every Delta table written by the cluster
In Unity Catalog data lineage graphs to track which cluster produced each output table
In Databricks audit logs as access-control events attached to each cluster start and stop

questions.explanation: Cluster tags propagate to Azure resource billing data. Teams use them to attribute cloud spend by environment, team, or cost center in Azure Cost Management. They do not affect permissions, table metadata, or lineage tracking.

questions.prompt: Your team must ingest JSON event files arriving continuously at ~1,000 files per minute from Azure Data Lake into a Delta table. Which ingestion approach is most appropriate and why?

options.label: COPY INTO — optimized for high-frequency streaming and tracks each file for exactly-once delivery
PySpark spark.read.json() in a scheduled Job — scales by parallelizing reads across Spark executors
Auto Loader with cloudFiles format — uses file notifications or incremental listing to track new files without rescanning the full directory each microbatch
Azure Data Factory Copy Activity — handles JSON natively and writes directly to Delta format without Databricks compute

questions.explanation: Auto Loader (cloudFiles) is designed for continuous file ingestion at scale. It tracks which files have been processed using Azure Event Grid notifications or incremental directory listing, avoiding expensive full-directory scans. COPY INTO is better suited for scheduled batch loads.

questions.prompt: Your Auto Loader pipeline has cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes enabled and a schemaLocation configured. After three months, source Parquet files begin including a new field temperature_c that was absent from the original schema. What does Auto Loader do on the next microbatch?

options.label: The pipeline fails immediately with a schema mismatch error and must be manually restarted with a schema reset flag
Detects the evolved schema, updates the checkpoint at schemaLocation, triggers a controlled stream restart to apply the new schema; prior rows receive NULL for the new column
Silently drops temperature_c to preserve backward schema compatibility with the existing Delta table
Promotes all existing columns to STRING to accommodate the new field without modifying the schema checkpoint

questions.explanation: Auto Loader detects schema evolution and updates the schema checkpoint. It raises a SchemaEvolutionException to trigger a controlled stream restart so the new schema is applied cleanly. After restart, existing rows get NULL for the new column and new rows include temperature_c.

questions.prompt: Which tools can orchestrate data movement into Databricks workloads?

Databricks Jobs
A local text editor only

questions.prompt: Your pipeline receives daily sales CSV files via COPY INTO. The source occasionally re-delivers the prior day's file with corrections using the same filename. What is the key limitation of COPY INTO when corrections arrive as re-delivered files with the same path?

options.label: COPY INTO re-reads all previously loaded files on every run, creating duplicates each time a file is re-delivered
COPY INTO tracks loaded files by path in the Delta transaction log; a re-delivered file with the same path is treated as already loaded and skipped, so corrections are silently ignored
COPY INTO cannot process CSV files from ADLS — Parquet or Delta format is required for cloud storage sources
COPY INTO requires a primary key column to detect corrections; without it the command is rejected at parse time

questions.explanation: COPY INTO maintains idempotency by tracking loaded file paths in the Delta transaction log. A corrected file reusing the same path is considered already loaded and skipped. For correction workflows, MERGE INTO is the appropriate approach as it can upsert based on a key.

questions.prompt: Your Spark Structured Streaming job aggregates click events into 5-minute tumbling windows. You add .withWatermark("event_time", "10 minutes") to handle late data. What does the 10-minute watermark specifically control?

options.label: The maximum delay between microbatches — if no new data arrives within 10 minutes the stream stops automatically
How long Spark retains intermediate aggregation state for open windows; events arriving more than 10 minutes past their window's close time are dropped
The checkpoint flush interval — state files older than 10 minutes are garbage-collected from the checkpoint directory
The trigger interval — the stream processes one microbatch every 10 minutes regardless of file arrival cadence

questions.explanation: A watermark tells Spark the maximum lateness it should tolerate. State for a 5-minute window is kept until the event-time clock advances past (window-end + 10 min). Events arriving after that threshold are dropped. The watermark also lets Spark safely clean up old state to bound memory usage.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at Solaris Energy building an Auto Loader pipeline to ingest turbine sensor CSV files. The pipeline runs successfully, but after adding 500 new files you observe that some files are processed twice. What is the most likely cause?

codeSnippet.code:
df_turbine = (spark.readStream
    .format("cloudFiles")
    .option("cloudFiles.format", "csv")
    .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation",
            "/checkpoints/solaris/schema")
    .load("abfss://raw@solarisstorage.dfs.core.windows.net/turbines/"))

(df_turbine.writeStream
    .format("delta")
    .option("checkpointLocation",
            "/checkpoints/solaris/bronze")
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start("abfss://bronze@solarisstorage.dfs.core.windows.net/turbines"))

options.label: trigger(availableNow=True) forces Auto Loader to replay all source files from the beginning on each run
The checkpointLocation was deleted or changed between runs, causing Auto Loader to lose track of which files were already processed
cloudFiles.format = 'csv' does not support incremental file tracking; only JSON and Parquet formats maintain file state
Delta Lake does not support idempotent appends — duplicate files must be deduplicated manually with MERGE INTO downstream

questions.explanation: Auto Loader tracks processed files using the checkpointLocation. If this path is deleted, moved, or changed between runs, Auto Loader loses its state and re-processes files it already loaded. trigger(availableNow=True) is safe and does not cause replays when the checkpoint is intact.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer ingesting daily real estate listing CSV files into a bronze Delta table. A scheduled job runs this statement twice in the same day due to a retry. What happens to the data in bronze.real_estate_listings on the second run?

codeSnippet.code:
COPY INTO bronze.real_estate_listings
FROM 'abfss://raw@realestatestorage.dfs.core.windows.net/listings/2024/'
FILEFORMAT = CSV
FORMAT_OPTIONS (
    'header' = 'true',
    'inferSchema' = 'true'
);

options.label: The second run truncates the target table and reloads all files from scratch
The second run raises a FilesAlreadyLoadedException and the job fails immediately
Only files not yet successfully loaded are ingested; already-processed files are skipped, making COPY INTO idempotent
Duplicate rows are inserted because COPY INTO does not track previously loaded files

questions.explanation: COPY INTO tracks which files have been successfully loaded in the Delta transaction log. Running it again is safe — new files are ingested and already-loaded files are skipped. This idempotency makes it reliable for scheduled batch jobs with retry logic.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at Solaris Energy. Your Auto Loader stream writes parsed turbine sensor readings to a silver Delta table. The cluster restarts mid-batch. After recovery, you observe no duplicate rows and no data loss. What makes exactly-once delivery possible?

codeSnippet.code:
(df_parsed
    .writeStream
    .format("delta")
    .outputMode("append")
    .option("checkpointLocation",
            "/checkpoints/solaris/silver-turbines")
    .trigger(availableNow=True)
    .start("abfss://silver@solarisstorage.dfs.core.windows.net/turbines"))

options.label: trigger(availableNow=True) replays only the last incomplete batch and discards any partial writes on cluster recovery
Delta Lake automatically locks the output path during recovery to prevent concurrent writes that could cause duplication
outputMode("append") deduplicates rows by matching them against existing Delta records on each restart
checkpointLocation stores committed source offsets and processed file state so the stream resumes exactly where it left off without reprocessing or losing data

questions.explanation: The checkpointLocation persists stream progress — which source offsets and files were committed. On restart, Spark reads this state and continues from the last successful commit, delivering exactly-once semantics when combined with Delta Lake's transactional writes.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at a real estate analytics company joining df_listings (8M rows), df_agents (200K rows), and df_zip_codes (800 rows). You apply a broadcast hint only to df_zip_codes. Join time drops from 5 minutes to 22 seconds. Why does broadcasting only df_zip_codes give the best result?

codeSnippet.code:
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast

df_result = (df_listings
    .join(df_agents, on="agent_id", how="left")
    .join(broadcast(df_zip_codes), on="zip_code", how="left"))

options.label: df_zip_codes fits in executor memory and is replicated to all workers, eliminating the shuffle of df_listings; broadcasting df_agents at 200K rows would risk executor OOM and negate the benefit
Spark allows only one broadcast hint per query; df_zip_codes is selected because it has the fewest columns
Broadcasting requires Delta Lake format; df_agents is stored as Parquet and cannot be broadcast automatically
df_agents has a surrogate primary key enabling an optimized sort-merge strategy that is faster than broadcasting for medium-sized tables

questions.explanation: A broadcast join copies the small table to every executor so the large table never shuffles across the network. An 800-row lookup is safe and eliminates an expensive Exchange stage. Attempting to broadcast a 200K-row table risks out-of-memory errors on executors and can be slower than a sort-merge join.

questions.prompt: You are a data engineer at a real estate analytics firm producing a quarterly average listing-price report. After running this transformation, what is the shape of df_quarterly compared with the original df_listings?

codeSnippet.code:
df_quarterly = (df_listings
    .groupBy("city")
    .pivot("quarter", ["Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"])
    .agg({"list_price": "avg"}))

df_quarterly.show()

options.label: Same row count as df_listings — pivot is a display transformation that does not change DataFrame structure
One row per (city, quarter) pair — same granularity as the original, sorted by quarter
One row per unique city with four new columns Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 each containing the average list price for that quarter
The DataFrame is transposed so city names become column headers and quarters become the row index

questions.explanation: Pivot rotates the distinct values of the pivot column (quarter) into separate output columns. The result has one row per city and four revenue columns (Q1–Q4) each containing the aggregated value, reducing row count compared to the original while widening the schema.

questions.prompt: The group analysts has SELECT on table main.sales.revenue. analysts is a child of group data_consumers, which also holds SELECT on the same table. You run REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE main.sales.revenue FROM GROUP analysts. Can members of analysts still query the table?

options.label: No — REVOKE propagates transitively through parent groups and removes inherited access as well
Yes — REVOKE removes only the direct grant from analysts; members who inherit SELECT through data_consumers retain access
No — Unity Catalog applies the most restrictive grant when a direct revoke conflicts with an inherited grant
Yes — but only until the next metastore sync, after which the inherited access is also revoked

questions.explanation: Revoking a privilege from a group removes only that direct grant. Users who belong to multiple groups retain access if another group still holds the privilege. Unity Catalog privilege evaluation is additive — the most permissive applicable grant wins.

questions.prompt: A service principal has SELECT on table prod.finance.invoices but no other Unity Catalog grants. It runs SELECT * FROM prod.finance.invoices and receives SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND. What privilege is missing?

options.label: Service principals cannot use SQL SELECT — they must call the Databricks REST API to read tables
SELECT on a managed table requires a separate EXTERNAL LOCATION grant for the underlying cloud storage path
USE CATALOG on prod and USE SCHEMA on prod.finance — without these the three-level namespace cannot be traversed
The SELECT grant must be approved by a workspace admin within 24 hours before it takes effect

questions.explanation: Unity Catalog namespace traversal requires USE CATALOG at the catalog level and USE SCHEMA at the schema level. Even with SELECT on the table, without these traversal privileges the SQL engine cannot resolve the fully qualified name.

)

df_events.cache()
df_events.count()  # materialise the cache
